comments.author: Ndancejic
comments.body:
I have a root-cause for the second crash reported with this signature:
```
2024 Dec 19 18:27:17.675064 r-tigon-21 ERR swss#orchagent: :- flush_setting_entries: EntityBulker.flush set entry attribute failed, number of entries to set: 1, status: SAI_STATUS_ITEM_NOT_FOUND
```

It's caused by muxOrch handling of tunnel route. When PortChannel is learned as a zero-mac neighbor, orchagent assigns a tunnel route to the Peer ToR to see if the peer has this neighbor learned. However if another route with a prefix matching this neighbor ip is learned and the neighbor mac is resolved in a short period of time, dualtor logic can remove the tunnel route before our internal cache is updated. The route update will then attempt to set route, but fail because it's not present in the ASIC. I'm discussing the plan for fix this week and will update that as soon as we figure out a plan/have a PR out.


# Bulker Stopping on single failure
bulk route removal fails on an unrelated route that does not exist:
```
2025 Mar 14 23:21:24.837827 str3-msn4700-12 ERR swss#orchagent: :- meta_sai_validate_route_entry: object key SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ROUTE_ENTRY:{"dest":"2.0.2.44/3

```


I don't see any failures for other routes, so I think one of the issues here is that the route bulk operation is failing on a single route and is not processing other routes that are left:
```
2025 Mar 14 23:21:24.837827 str3-msn4700-12 ERR swss#orchagent: :- meta_sai_validate_route_entry: object key SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ROUTE_ENTRY:{"dest":"2.0.2.44/32","switch_id":"oid:0x21000000000000","vr":"oid:0x3000000000002"} doesn't exist
2025 Mar 14 23:21:24.837847 str3-msn4700-12 ERR swss#orchagent: :- flush_removing_entries: EntityBulker.flush remove entries failed, number of entries to remove: 326, status: SAI_STATUS_ITEM_NOT_FOUND
...
2025 Mar 14 23:21:24.839708 str3-msn4700-12 ERR swss#orchagent: :- removeRoutePost: Failed to remove route prefix:2.0.1.0/32
2025 Mar 14 23:21:24.839735 str3-msn4700-12 NOTICE swss#orchagent: :- removeRoutePost: Remove Nexthop Group 2.0.1.0@PortChannel101,2.0.0.1@PortChannel101
2025 Mar 14 23:21:24.839735 str3-msn4700-12 INFO swss#orchagent: :- isMuxNexthops: No mux nexthop found
2025 Mar 14 23:21:24.839735 str3-msn4700-12 INFO swss#orchagent: :- removeRoutePost: Remove route 2.0.1.0/32 with next hop(s) 2.0.1.0@PortChannel101,2.0.0.1@PortChannel101
```


Looks like the routes do not get processed and therefore return task_success, which causes orchagent to believe that it is safe to remove route references, otherwise it would return and not process the nexthop group. However, entitybulker is currently configured to ignore ERROR and continue processing removal entries, I don't think this is happening in this case:
routeorch.cpp:
```
if (status != SAI_STATUS_SUCCESS)
{
    SWSS_LOG_ERROR("Failed to remove route prefix:%s\n", ipPrefix.to_string().c_str());
    task_process_status handle_status = handleSaiRemoveStatus(SAI_API_ROUTE, status);
    if (handle_status != task_success)
    {
        return parseHandleSaiStatusFailure(handle_status);
    }
}
```


bulker.h:
```
sai_status_t status = (*remove_entries)((uint32_t)count, rs.data(), SAI_BULK_OP_ERROR_MODE_IGNORE_ERROR, statuses.data());
```

# Route failure
The reason the route is failing to be removed is that the nexthop for this IP is unresolved when the route is added because neighbor creation has not been processed yet:
```

...
2025 Mar 14 23:18:24.818648 str3-msn4700-12 INFO swss#orchagent: :- addRoutePost: Post create route 2.0.1.0/32 with next hop(s) 2.0.0.1@PortChannel101
2025 Mar 14 23:18:24.818648 str3-msn4700-12 INFO swss#orchagent: :- isMuxNexthops: No mux nexthop found
```
After some time, a zero mac neighbor entry is created to check if peer has this neighbor resolved. Since the neighbor is not resolved before test cleanup, the tunnel route is removed:
```
2025 Mar 14 23:18:39.645932 str3-msn4700-12 INFO swss#orchagent: :- addZeroMacTunnelRoute: Creating tunnel route for neighbor 2.0.2.44
2025 Mar 14 23:18:39.645932 str3-msn4700-12 INFO swss#orchagent: :- createStandaloneTunnelRoute: Creating standalone tunnel route for neighbor 2.0.2.44
2025 Mar 14 23:18:39.645932 str3-msn4700-12 ERR swss#orchagent: :- meta_sai_validate_route_entry: object key SAI_OBJECT_TYPE_ROUTE_ENTRY:{"dest":"2.0.2.44/32","switch_id":"oid:0x21000000000000","vr":"oid:0x3000000000002"} already exists
2025 Mar 14 23:18:39.645932 str3-msn4700-12 NOTICE swss#orchagent: :- create_route: Tunnel route to 2.0.2.44/32 already exists
```

So when this route is being processed, the entry is not present in asic which leads to SAI_STATUS_ITEM_NOT_FOUND error.

# Summary
I think there's two issues going on here:
1. the bulker should be processing all remove_entry operations, even if SAI_STATUS_ITEM_NOT_FOUND is returned for a single entity. @dprital could you help confirm that the bulk operations are handling SAI_BULK_OP_ERROR_MODE_IGNORE_ERROR flag correctly? If so, and there is really an error with the remaining remove_entry operations, could you help confirm why handleSaiRemoveStatus is returning task_success code?
2. routeOrch is unaware of tunnel routes created in dualtor cases (either from muxorch or StandaloneTunnelRoute) and conflicting route entries will get processed without knowledge of tunnel routes being created or removed. I'm already working on a fix for this as mentioned above, but this is a slightly different case that I'll make sure to add to testing.

>  @dprital could you help confirm that the bulk operations are handling SAI_BULK_OP_ERROR_MODE_IGNORE_ERROR flag correctly?


comments.body:
There's 4 things here that each individually contributed to the test case failure:

1. Expected neighbor entry missing from kernel, causing tunnel-route to be programmed for unresolved nexthop.
2. tunnel-route being removed when nexthop group was deleted
3. route bulker ending early due to ITEM_NOT_FOUND (not processing remaining bulk removes)
4. next-hop group delete failing due to OBJECT_IN_USE causing crash.

For 1: Created a PR that will process the neighbor creation step in batches to prevent the entries from being dropped in the kernel. This eventually leads to the crash because of 2-4. I think we need to understand why this is happening specifically on SN4700 devices (is there some buffer that's overflowing?) Other than that none of the issues seem to be platform specific.

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/19003

For 2: I need to look into some options here, the issue happens when we have a route with a missing nexthop. dualtor logic programs a tunnel-route, but this can conflict with the existing route.

For 3: I'll open a PR to address this. You were right, this is happening in syncd and needs to be fixed in syncd.

For 4: We have a PR coming out for orchagent that will handle OBJECT_IN_USE errors. I'll update when that's out.

linkedPullRequests.title: [crm] Fix test failures on SN4700 by batching neighbor creation
linkedPullRequests.author: Ndancejic
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR
test_crm_nexthop_group was failing on sn4700 testbeds due to a known orchagent crash. The crash is caused by a few factors:

- Expected neighbor entry missing from kernel, causing tunnel-route to be programmed for unresolved nexthop.
- tunnel-route being removed when nexthop group was deleted
- route bulker ending early due to ITEM_NOT_FOUND (not processing remaining bulk removes)
- next-hop group delete failing due to OBJECT_IN_USE.

This PR addresses the first issue.

During neighbor generation for the test, some of the neighbor updates were being missed from APPL_DB on sn4700 devices. Previously, the neighbors were programmed in the kernel in a single ip command, this fix splits up the neighbor programming into batches in order to prevent updates from being dropped.

Summary:
Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/21243

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)

- [ ] Test case improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
CRM test was failing on dualtor sn4700 platforms

#### How did you do it?
buffered neighbor creation to prevent updates from being dropped

#### How did you verify/test it?
ran test case on sn4700 dualto testbed

#### Any platform specific information?
only changes test run on sn4700

comments.author: bingwang-ms
comments.body: @Ndancejic Can you help me understand `During neighbor generation for the test, some of the neighbor updates were being missed from APPL_DB on sn4700 devices.` ? Is it possible that doing it in batch hides some real issue?

comments.author: Ndancejic
comments.body:
> @Ndancejic Can you help me understand `During neighbor generation for the test, some of the neighbor updates were being missed from APPL_DB on sn4700 devices.` ? Is it possible that doing it in batch hides some real issue?

I noticed that some of the neighbor entries being added at the start of the test were not being notified in appdb. appdb gets these from netlink when programming neighbors through the kernel. From what I understand if there's a high volume, these can be dropped from the kernel sometimes. In this case we were programming ~2000 entries in a single `ip neigh replace` command
